sentences.text: In 1925, a brilliant con artist pulled off the most impossible heist in history.
He sold the Eiffel Tower for scrap metal—without owning a single bolt.
Reading that Paris couldn't afford the tower's repairs, he forged official ministry papers.
He secretly invited six greedy scrap-metal dealers to a luxury suite at Hotel de Crillon.
He claimed the city was quietly demolishing the tower, and targeted one insecure dealer: André Poisson.
When Poisson grew suspicious, Lustig played his psychological masterstroke.
He subtly hinted that as an underpaid clerk, he needed a personal bribe.
In France, corrupt bureaucrats were normal—a bribe proved the deal was real.
Poisson handed over a suitcase of cash, and Lustig boarded a train to Vienna.
Poisson was so humiliated he never went to the police.
Months later, Lustig returned to Paris to sell the Eiffel Tower a second time!
Master con artists never sell impossible lies.
They simply sell people what their greed wants to believe.
